scenarios.title: Scope response exposes service-desc discovery

requirements.selectedText: An ordinary `GET` of the Scope URI MUST return a successful response carrying a registered [`service-desc` link relation](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8631.html) to the machine-readable JSON discovery document.

scenarios.title: Read discovery has the exact required and prohibited members

requirements.selectedText: `bdpVersion`, `profile`, `scope`, `beads`, `links`, and `types` are required in every profile. `operations` is required in Read+Update and Transactional and prohibited in Read.

The optional
`order` member names the collection order under
[Collection retrieval and selection](#collection-retrieval-and-selection);
omission means the `canonical-uri` baseline.

scenarios.title: Discovery navigation is canonical and Scope-confined

requirements.selectedText: For the canonical Scope URL `S`, `beads` MUST equal the URL produced by resolving `beads/` against `S`, `links` MUST equal `links/` resolved against `S`, and `types` MUST equal `types/` resolved against `S`.

scenarios.title: Advertised Read limits are valid and binding

requirements.selectedText: Omission means only that the bound is not pre-advertised; it does not mean infinite capacity and does not permit silent truncation, partial mutation, or a non-normative failure response.

scenarios.title: Generic clients reject unsupported versions and profiles

requirements.selectedText: Profile negotiation MUST begin with Scope discovery and MUST reject unsupported BDP versions rather than guessing compatibility.

scenarios.title: Individual Bead reads return complete canonical records

requirements.selectedText: Every successful `GET` of a Bead or Link returns one self-contained Resource record.
A successful Resource read returns the complete stored properties object, including properties not declared by any effective schema, and an update preserves every untouched property.

scenarios.title: Individual Link reads return complete canonical records

requirements.selectedText: Every successful `GET` of a Bead or Link returns one self-contained Resource record.

scenarios.title: Link endpoint References stay opaque and pin-faithful

requirements.selectedText: Any Reference may carry a pin: an authority MUST preserve and echo the pin byte-identically, MUST compare it only for equality, and MUST NOT validate, dereference, or interpret it in v0.
Every Link endpoint MUST be a Reference: a URI, or a Pinned Reference with exactly `uri` and `revision`.
An in-Scope endpoint MUST identify a live Bead by its canonical URL.
At least one endpoint of every v0 Link MUST be an in-Scope Bead.

A Bead whose
  Type owns outgoing Link Types MUST carry its `ownedLinks` member — one
  entry per declared owned type, keyed by Link Type URL, valued by the
  owned Links' complete records in ascending code-unit order of their
  canonical `id`s — on every record read, and the member MUST be absent
  for Beads whose Type owns nothing.

scenarios.title: Properties views return the complete open properties object

requirements.selectedText: `view=properties` is valid for both Beads and Links and returns exactly the complete stored `properties` object:

scenarios.title: Default Bead reads do not embed incident Links

requirements.selectedText: The default Bead `GET` remains bounded and does not include Links.

scenarios.title: Unknown, deleted, and non-visible Resources share one response

requirements.selectedText: After a Bead or Link is deleted, ordinary `GET`, `view=properties`, and, for a Bead, `view=links` return the same `404` `resource-not-found` problem used for an unknown or non-visible identity.

scenarios.title: Type inventory returns paginated exact summaries

requirements.selectedText: Each page is an object containing `items` and `next`; each item is exactly the Type summary `{id, name, describes}`.

scenarios.title: Controlled Type publishers return closed descriptors

requirements.selectedText: Descriptor objects and endpoint-constraint objects are closed: no members are allowed except those defined above.

scenarios.title: Generic Resource reads do not require descriptor retrieval

requirements.selectedText: A generic client MUST be able to parse and issue protocol requests without retrieving a Type Descriptor.

scenarios.title: Bead collection returns complete records and continuation

requirements.selectedText: An ordinary `GET` of a discovered collection returns a paginated `items` array and a `next` URL.

The baseline order every authority MUST support is
`canonical-uri` — ascending lexicographic comparison, by Unicode code
unit, of each item's absolute canonical `id`.

scenarios.title: Link collection returns complete records and continuation

requirements.selectedText: The `beads/` and `links/` collections return complete Resource records; the `types/` collection returns Type summaries.

The baseline order every authority MUST support is
`canonical-uri` — ascending lexicographic comparison, by Unicode code
unit, of each item's absolute canonical `id`.

scenarios.title: Collection structural predicates compose exactly

requirements.selectedText: Different predicates are combined with logical AND. Within `endpoint`, source and target are combined with logical OR.

scenarios.title: Bounded Selector evaluates over canonical candidate records

requirements.selectedText: The structural predicates and Selector decide the complete matching set before pagination, but only within the request's Authorization View.

scenarios.title: Collection continuations preserve one logical snapshot

requirements.selectedText: A cursor continues one logical projected snapshot: every page belongs to the same selected set, authorization projection, and Resource revisions as the initial request.

scenarios.title: Expired and foreign-view cursors fail without restart

requirements.selectedText: If the authority can no longer continue the snapshot, or if the request no longer belongs to that projection, it returns an expired- or foreign-view-cursor problem rather than silently restarting against newer state.

scenarios.title: Unsupported and repeated collection parameters are rejected

requirements.selectedText: A parameter may occur at most once in BDP v0; repeated parameters are errors rather than implicit unions.

scenarios.title: Incident Link direction selection and default are exact

requirements.selectedText: `direction` is `inbound`, `outbound`, or `both`, and defaults to `both` when omitted.

scenarios.title: Incident Link continuations preserve one snapshot

requirements.selectedText: As with collection pagination, that continuation walks one logical snapshot and an expired cursor is an error rather than a silent restart against newer state.

scenarios.title: Application resources support GET and HEAD

requirements.selectedText: An implementation advertising the `read` profile MUST support `GET` and `HEAD` for application requests.

scenarios.title: Unsupported methods receive 405 without a BDP Problem representation

requirements.selectedText: Every such `405` MUST include `Allow: GET, HEAD`, plus `OPTIONS` when cross-origin access is enabled, and MUST NOT include a BDP Problem body.

scenarios.title: Every Read Problem preserves its status, family, code, and retry row

requirements.selectedText: Each code fixes its HTTP status and retry disposition. The Read profile uses this closed table:

scenarios.title: Unexpected internal faults are body-less and redacted

requirements.selectedText: An implementation MUST respond to an unexpected internal server fault with a body-less `500 Internal Server Error`, MUST NOT include a BDP Problem body, and MUST keep internal fault details off the wire.

scenarios.title: Read caching and optional CORS fields are observable

requirements.selectedText: Scope-bounded representations that depend on authorization use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

scenarios.title: Raw invalid request targets cannot bypass Scope identity

requirements.selectedText: Empty, `.`, and `..` segments, controls, backslashes, queries, fragments, scheme-relative references, and encoded `/` or `\` separators are invalid.

scenarios.title: Coverage diagnostic for disconnect recovery

requirements.selectedText: The matrix MUST cover positive, negative, profile, concurrency, disconnect, expiry, restore, and cross-implementation cases applicable to each profile.

scenarios.title: Restore preserves identity or moves to a new Scope URL

requirements.selectedText: A restore that cannot preserve that guarantee creates a different logical Scope and therefore uses a different canonical Scope URL.

scenarios.title: Coverage diagnostic for malformed client responses

requirements.selectedText: The conformance kit MUST validate normative schemas and observable semantics independently of the server implementation wherever practical, reducing common-mode defects.

scenarios.title: Portability diagnostic for cross-target fixture equivalence

requirements.selectedText: Tests exercise public HTTP behavior and consume the normative schema bundle; they do not inspect an implementation's storage or internal server interfaces.

scenarios.title: Alias URLs resolve with one redirect and disclose nothing

requirements.selectedText:
a `GET` or `HEAD` of an alias URL —
`alias/{alias-path}` resolved against the canonical Scope URL — returns
`307 Temporary Redirect` with `Location` set to the target's absolute
canonical Bead URL and no body.

An unknown alias, an alias URL carrying a query or fragment, and any alias
URL at an authority that does not advertise `aliases` return the same `404`
`resource-not-found` used for unknown Resources

Alias resolution MUST be
  redirect-only: `GET` and `HEAD` return `307` with `Location` set to the
  target's absolute canonical Bead URL and no body.

scenarios.title: An alias-less authority discloses nothing at alias URLs

requirements.selectedText:
An unknown alias, an alias URL carrying a query or fragment, and any alias
URL at an authority that does not advertise `aliases` return the same `404`
`resource-not-found` used for unknown Resources

An unknown alias returns
  the same `404` `resource-not-found` as an unknown Resource. An authority
  without aliases omits the `aliases` discovery member.

scenarios.title: Authorized disclosure distinguishes pruned from erased

requirements.selectedText:
A
`resource-pruned` problem MAY carry one `archivedAt` member — a Reference,
possibly pinned, naming where the content went

A
`resource-erased` problem carries no condition-specific extension members
beyond its ordinary problem members: even a pointer would disclose what
erasure exists to remove.

scenarios.title: Disclosure is authorization-gated, never an enumeration oracle

requirements.selectedText:
To every other caller all
three conditions remain the uniform `404`; the disclosure vocabulary is
never an enumeration oracle.

Unauthorized callers MUST receive the uniform
  `404` `resource-not-found`.

scenarios.title: Views are closed over owned Links

requirements.selectedText:
Because the member is covered, it is never authorization-filtered. An
Authorization View that projects a Bead projects its owned Links and
their in-Scope target Beads: a view is closed over owned Links, and
hiding a Bead from a view therefore requires hiding every Bead that owns
a Link to it.

An Authorization View that projects
  a Bead projects its owned Links and their in-Scope targets.

scenarios.title: Records carry attribution as data, not evidence

requirements.selectedText:
Every Bead and Link record MAY carry an **`attribution`** member: a
common, generic member in a common place, so that no Type has to declare
attribution as a domain property.

It is outside `properties`, never part of
the `properties` view

Bead and Link records MAY carry a common `attribution`
  member — `{ principal, status }` with `status` one of `claimed`,
  `unknown` — that is carried per version and never attested

scenarios.title: Link records carry attribution beside revision

requirements.selectedText:
Every Bead and Link record MAY carry an **`attribution`** member: a
common, generic member in a common place, so that no Type has to declare
attribution as a domain property.

It is outside `properties`, never part of
the `properties` view

scenarios.title: A Bead Type Descriptor may own every outgoing Link Type through the wildcard entry

requirements.selectedText: `ownsOutgoing` MAY also contain the **wildcard entry** `"*"`, whose value is exactly `{ max }`: it declares every outgoing Link Type not listed explicitly as owned.
The wildcard MAY be the only entry.

The key MAY also be the wildcard `"*"`, whose value is exactly `{ max }`: it owns every outgoing Link Type not named explicitly, its `max` bounds the whole owned set, and explicit entries take precedence for the types they name, under [Owned Links](#owned-links). A Link Type Descriptor must not carry `ownsOutgoing`.
A Bead Type's `ownsOutgoing` MAY carry the wildcard entry `"*"` — exactly `{ max }` — owning every outgoing Link Type not named explicitly

scenarios.title: The wildcard entry is exactly { max }

requirements.selectedText: Each declaration MUST carry `max`, the largest owned set the Type permits.
The wildcard entry carries no `label`: it names no Link Type.

Descriptor objects and endpoint-constraint objects are closed: no members are allowed except those defined above. An `ownsOutgoing` entry is closed the same way: `{ label?, max }` under a Link Type URL, `{ max }` under the wildcard.

scenarios.title: An explicitly declared entry's max does not exceed the wildcard's max in the same descriptor

requirements.selectedText: An explicitly declared entry's `max` therefore MUST NOT exceed the wildcard's `max` in the same descriptor — the excess could never be reached — and a descriptor that declares one is invalid: descriptor validation refuses it, and the Type is not installed.
That rule compares two members, which the schema bundle cannot express; it is a descriptor-validation rule beyond the schema, and a descriptor the bundle accepts can still fail it.

An explicitly declared entry's `max` MUST NOT exceed the wildcard's `max` in the same descriptor, since the wildcard's `max` bounds the whole owned set: such a descriptor is invalid and is not installed — a descriptor-validation rule beyond the schema bundle, which cannot compare the two members — under [Owned Links](#owned-links).

scenarios.title: A wildcard owner's ownedLinks carries present types plus empty explicit entries, never the wildcard

requirements.selectedText: The member carries one entry for each owned Link Type actually present on the Bead — at least one owned Link of that type exists — plus an entry, possibly empty, for each explicitly declared Link Type; a Link Type owned only through the wildcard has an entry exactly when an owned Link of that type is present.
The wildcard `"*"` is never a key: the member is keyed by Link Type URL alone.
The member is present, possibly empty, for every Bead whose Type carries `ownsOutgoing`, and absent for Beads whose Type owns nothing.

A Bead whose Type owns outgoing Link Types additionally carries its `ownedLinks` member — one entry per owned Link Type present on the Bead and one, possibly empty, per explicitly declared Link Type, keyed by the Link Type URL and never by the wildcard `"*"`, valued by the owned Links' complete records in ascending code-unit order of their canonical `id`s — on every record read; the member is absent for Beads whose Type owns nothing.
the `ownedLinks` member of such a Bead MUST carry one entry per owned Link Type present plus an empty entry per explicitly declared type, keyed by Link Type URL and never by `"*"`.

scenarios.title: A view is closed over wildcard-owned Links

requirements.selectedText: Because the member is covered, it is never authorization-filtered. An Authorization View that projects a Bead projects its owned Links and their in-Scope target Beads: a view is closed over owned Links, and hiding a Bead from a view therefore requires hiding every Bead that owns a Link to it.

For a wildcard owner the consequence is stated plainly, because it is the price of inline, revision-covered references: such a Bead owns every outgoing Link it makes, so a Bead that owns a Link to a Bead hidden from a view is hidden from that view too — a Memory that cites a hidden Bead is hidden with it.

A visible Bead need not expose hidden incident Links — a latitude confined to incoming and unowned Links: a visible source's owned Links, covered by its revision, are never withheld, and the view includes their in-Scope targets, under [Owned Links](#owned-links).

scenarios.title: A content-derived revision-token scheme declares its number model by name

requirements.selectedText: A revision-token scheme that derives tokens from content MUST declare, by name, the number model it serializes under: `sha256-jcs` means RFC 8785 serialization with numbers as binary64 under its Section 3.2.2.3, and is exact over admitted values by construction; a scheme over exact decimals is a different scheme with a different name.
On every admitted value the exact-decimal model and the binary64 model agree by construction.
a content-derived revision-token scheme MUST declare its number model by name, and `sha256-jcs` names RFC 8785 serialization with numbers as binary64.
